resources.title: Meaning of Agriculture
resources.description: Theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Meaning of Agriculture: - growing of crops like corn, rice, guinea corn, cassava - rearing of animals like chicken, pig, goat, cattle - processing and selling of agricultural products 2. Importance of agriculture: - as source of food - Income generation - as job or employment - for producing industrial raw materials - for cloth making, - medicines etc. 3. People in agriculture: - animal rearers - crop farmers - fishermen - market people - gardeners - agriculture teachers. 4. Displays live samples in class.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define agriculture. 2. list the importance of agriculture in Nigeria. iii. identify people involved in agricultural activities.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of agriculture. 2. Guides the pupils to mention activities that can build up the definition in a broad sense. 3. Guides pupils to mention the importance of agriculture in Nigeria. Explain briefly each of the importance named. 4. Asks pupils to name different activities that people engaged in agriculture do. 5. Explains the role performed by each group of people named. 6. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Pupils suggest definition of agriculture. 2. Mention what they know as the importance of agriculture to the community. 3. List the different activities that people engaged in agriculture do in their localities. 4. identify the various crops displayed 5. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. Pictorial display of people planting crop, rearing animals, processing agricultural products, selling agricultural products. 2. Simple chart or pictures showing the importance of Agriculture in Nigeria. 3. Live samples of some crops produce.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define Agriculture. 2. mention four importance of agriculture in Nigeria. 3. mention five groups of people involved in agriculture.

resources.title: Soil Types and Enrichment
resources.description: Theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Meaning of soil 2. Soil classification day, Sandy and loamy. 3. Causes of soil fertility reduction: - burning - leaching - overgrazing - clean clearing - erosion, etc. 4. Ways of making the soil fertile: - adding fertilizer - manuring - mulching - crop rotation - leaving fallow.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define soil 2. list soil types. 3. mention the causes of soil fertility reduction 4. describe ways of enriching soil fertility. 5. maintain the soil fertility of the school farm.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Collects soil samples to show their characteristics 2. Performs simple soil experiments to show their properties. 3. Guides soil fertility discussions 4. Collects samples of fertile soil (loam) and non-fertile soil (sand) in separate pots. 5.Plants maize in the pots to illustrate effect of soil fertility level on the plants. 6.Give a board summary

Students: 1. Observe and identify soil types. 2. Collect different soil types and note their differences. 3. Participate in class discussions. 4. Participate in carrying out the experiments set up by the teacher. 5. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. Soil samples: - sandy, clayey & loamy 2. Funnel 3. Water 4. Measuring glass 5. Filter paper 6. Cotton wool 7. Pots, 8. Maize grains
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define soil. 2. identify soil types. 3. state the best soil for growing crops. 4. explain what makes the soil to loose its fertility. 5. describe various methods involved in enriching the soil.

resources.title: Agricultural Tools and Equipment
resources.description: Theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: INTRODUCTION AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Farm tools: - Cutting tools e.g. cutlass, sickle, axe, etc. - Digging tools e.g. hoe, pick axe, spade, etc. - Carrying tools e.g. basket, head pan, wheel barrow, etc. - Gathering tools e.g. rake. 2. Animal farm tools: - fishing nets, traps, hook and line, baskets, watering troughs, feeding troughs, etc. 3. Maintenance and care of the tools: - store in a cool dry place - wash/clean and dry - rub oil on metal ends to avoid rusting - sharpening blunt edges, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1i. name farm tools. 2. identify and describe the tools and their uses. 3. maintain the tools after use.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays the tools in class. 2. Helps pupils to identify farm tools and their uses. 3. Demonstrates the use of farm tools. 4. Demonstrates proper maintenance of farm tools. 5. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Identify and narrate the uses of farm tools. 2. Use some farm tools on the school farm. 3. Carry out proper maintenance of tools after use. 4. copy board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Different farm tools e.g. hoe, cutlass, spade, shovel, rake, pick axe, wheelbarrow, fishing nets, hook and line, baskets, watering troughs, feeding troughs, etc. 2. Poster, charts and pictures of farm tools
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list 4 farm tools. 2. state the uses of hoe, hand trowel, rake, matchet, on the farm, fishing net, hook and line. 3. mention the uses of wheel barrow, watering can, head pan in the farm. 4. maintain farm tools.

resources.title: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Home Economics
resources.description: Theme: INTRODUCTION TO HOME ECONOMICS | Sub-theme: INTRODUCTION TO HOME ECONOMICS | Content: 1. Meaning of Home Economics. 2. Scope (Areas) of Home Economics. 3. Careers in Home Economics. 4. Importance of Home Economics to the society.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define and explain the meaning of Home Economics 2. enumerate the different areas of Home Economics 3. list various careers in Home Economics 4. outline the importance of Home Economics to the society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines and explains the meaning of Home Economics. 2. Enumerates the scope of Home Economics 3. Lists the careers in Home enonomics 4. Explains the importance of Home Economics to the society 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion. 2. Ask and answer questions. 3. Give examples of people in Home Economics careers 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Chart showing the scope and careers in Home Economics. 2. Chart and pictures illustrating careers in Home Economics, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define and explain the meaning of Home Economics; 2. list three areas of Home Economics; 3. mention five careers in Home Economics; 4. explain five reasons for the importance of Home Economics to the society

resources.title: Personal Grooming and Use of Basic Cosmetics
resources.description: Theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Parts of the human body: i. head: hair, eyes, nose, mouth, teeth, ear, neck, nose. ii. trunk: chest, arm, belly, pubic region,. iii. Limb: legs: legs, hands, with nails. 2. Functions of each part 3. Classify materials used for the care of the body, stating their uses. 4. Reasons for daily care of the body 5. Care for each part of the body. 6. Correct use of basic and safe cosmetics. 7. Adverse effects of some chemicals used in cosmetics.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify parts of the human body; 2. state functions of the parts of human body. 3. enumerate the tradiitional and modern materials used for taking care of the body and their uses. 4. demonstrate how to take care of the body. 5. use basic and safe cosmetics correctly
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays a properly labelled chart of parts of the body. 2. Discusses reasons for taking care of the body; 3. Brings all materials for taking care of the body to show pupils 4. Displays different materials for taking care of the body on table including traditional ones e.g.cam-wood or “uhie" (Igbo) or “osun” (Yoruba). antimony or Otajele (Igbo) or Tiroo (Yoruba”’ laali” (Yoruba) “lalle”(Hausa). 5. Displays other cosmetics e.g. oils. creams, pomades, powder, nail/polish, body spray, perfume, lipsticks, eye pencil. 6. Classify cosmetics into safe and dangerous cosmetics 7. Explains directions on labels 8. Demonstrates the correct use of each costmetics on the body. 9. Gives board summary

Students: 1. Touch different parts of their own body; 2. Display their finger, toe, nails for inspection; 3. Observe clean nails, clean clothing. 4. Differentiate between traditional and modern materials for the care of the body. 5. Identify information on containers of cosmetics e.g. use, expiry date, making list of ingredients. Bring empty containers of costemics containing lables 6. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. A labelled diagram of the body. 2. Soap, towel, sponge, water, tooth paste and brush, chewing stick, etc 3. Traditional and modern cosmetics; 4. Baby doll; 5. Labelled chat of safe and harsh or dangerous cosmetics.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify different parts of the body and their uses 2. state how to wash their body; 3. name materials for cleaning the body; 4. identify clean pupils; 5. identify different basic and safe cosmetics for good grooming. 6. use baby doll to demonstrate the care of different body parts. 7. mention one side effect of harsh cosmetics

resources.title: Types and Care of Personal Clothing
resources.description: Theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Types of personal clothing: shirts, blouses, skirts, pants, trousers, vests, scarves, wrappers, pyjamas, nightgown, footwears, caps etc. 2. Reasons for wearing clothing: i. protection ii. beauty iii. identification/status iv.for special occasions e.g. party 3. Laundry agents, tools and equipment: i. agent eg water, soap/detergents ii. tools eg basin, bath iii. equipment eg Iron washing machine 4. Steps in care of clothes i. washing ii. ironing iii. airing iv. storing
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify types of personal clothing; 2. mention reasons for wearing clothes and footwears; 3. state the reasons for caring for clothing 4. mention the steps in care of clothing 5. demonstrate how to care for shoes/bags e.g polishing 6. launder personal cloth.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays a variety of personal clothing/ items. 2. Produces a chart of variety of personal clothing articles. 3. Discusses the reasons for wearing clothes, and care of clothing articles 4. Provides pictures of people of various professions in uniforms e.g. i. nurses ii. police iii. fire service etc. 5. Demonstrates steps for caring of personal clothinarg 6. Gives board a summary

Students: 1. Identify and name different kinds of clothing 2. Practice how to hang and store their clothes and reasons for wearing clothes 3. Identify different people from the pictures according to their type of clothing. 4. State the materials needed for taking care of cothes. 5. Demonstrate how to launder clothes. 6. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Different articles of clothing 2. Laundry agents e.g soap, water, detergent, etc. 3. Laundry tools and equipment e.g. irons, line/rope for hanging clothes to dry, basin, pegs
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state three reasons for caring for clothes; 2. mention three materials for laundering clothes; 3. explain steps in laundering of clothes 4. launder a personal clothing

resources.title: Food: Classification and Functions of Food
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Meaning of food 2. Classification of foods and their sources 3. Classes of food nutrients and their functions 4. Explain an adequate diet 5. Deficiency diseases of each nutrient
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define food. 2. state reasons for eating food 3. list the six classes of food and their uses 4. mention classes of food nutrient 5. explain the functions of each food nutrient 6. mention deficiency diseases of nutrients
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines food and states reasons for eating of food 2. Discusses the types of food nutrients, sources and their functions with the pupils. 3. Provides real food items and chart of the classes of food based on their nutrients. 4. Displays charts and discusses deficiency diseases of nutrients. 5. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Define food 2. Observe the chart on display. 3. Classify the real food items on display 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Charts on food groups 2. Real food items 3. Charts on food nutrients, sources and functions 4. Pictures of people affected with deficiency of nutrients e.g. marasmus.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define food. 2. explain five reasons for eating food 3. list the six classes of food and one source each. 4. state one function of each food nutrient. 5. mention two deficiency diseases associated with food.

resources.title: How to Grow Crops
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Examples of crops: cereals, legumes, tubers. 2. Procedure for raising farm crops: a). Pre-planting activities: - land clearing and stumping, - preparing nursery beds and sowing. - selection and transplanting seedlings, - planting locally grown crops on ridges and beds in the school farm. b). Post planting activities: - watering, mulching, thinning and supplying, - application of fertilizer/manure. - weeding, - staking (where applicable), - application of pesticides, -harvesting of mature crops. 3. Post-Harvesting Activities: - processing/ preservation, - storage, - marketing. 4. Safety signs, symbols, labels e.g.: - skull and crossbones - chemical warning labels - treated seeds - veterinary drugs - implements, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. give examples of crops. 2. narrate and demonstrate the processes involved in raising crops. 3. raise seedlings of some vegetables and flowers in the nursery. 4. transplant seedlings from nursery to the field. 5. identify safety signs, labels and symbols on agricultural inputs
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to raise either a cereal or legume or tuber crops during the growing season. 2. Supplies appropriate tools and planting materials. 3 Takes pupils to the school farm and maps out the area to use for the year. 4. Allows pupils to prepare land themselves. 5. Guides pupils in identifying and explaining safety signs, labels and symbols on agricultural inputs before and during planting, harvesting activities, including safe handling of treated seeds, veterinary drugs, implements, etc. 6. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Bring the required farm tools from home. 2. Prepare the land for planting. 3. Plant seeds in the nursery and transplant to the field. 4. Care for the farm themselves.. 5. Carry out planting activities as directed by the teacher. 6. Pupils keep farm records 7. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. School farm.. 2. Farm tools. e.g. tape, machetes, hoes, spades, pegs, digging fork, hand trowel, knapsack sprayer, etc 3. Planting materials and inputs. such as. seeds of vegetables e.g. pepper, okra garden egg, onions, fluted pumpkin, tomato, rice, maize, millet, guinea corn, potato & yam sets, cassava cuttings. 4. Fertilizer/ manure pesticides. 5. charts of safety signs and symbols. 6. samples of labels.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list three crops grown in your area. 2. state the various activities involved in growing a named field crop. 3. grow any field crop from land clearing to marketing. 4. demonstrate how to transplant seedlings. 5. care and maintain the school farm. 6. harvest crops when mature. 7. keep records of farm activities performed 8. Explain 2 safety signs or symbols on agricultural inputs. 9. Bring 2 labels on agricultural inputs.

resources.title: Control of Crop Weeds, Pests and Diseases
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Definition and identification of weeds. 2. Problems of weeds to farmers. 3. Control measures: - biological - cultural - chemical 4. Pests: a) Meaning, and Identification b) Identification of insects pests, - Beetle/weevil, - Grasshopper/locust, - Caterpillar, - Termite. c). Other pests on: - rodents, - quela birds, - bats, - monkeys. 5. Damages caused by pests: - eat crop leaves & - roots - destroy grains, - damaging stalk, fruits and roots of crops - Contaminating stored produce.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define weeds and name some common local weeds. 2. state the problem of weeds to farmers. 3. control weeds in the farm. 4. define and identify common pests on our farm. 5. describe the damages caused by pests. 6. state ways of controlling pests. 7. list the causes of plant diseases. 8. state how the diseases can be controlled.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to define and identify common weeds on the environment. 2. Discusses problems created by weeds on farms. 3. Discusses control measures and their side effects. 4. Displays and identifies samples of: - fresh or preserved pest. - partly eaten/damaged vegetable leaves - Weevilled maize, beans guinea corn. 5. Displays charts and posters of rodents, birds, squirrels, grass-cutters, rats. 6. Discusses how to prevent or avoid eating contaminated food.

Students: 1. Make a weed album 2.Observe and identity pests 3. Observe and describe the damages done to crops by pests. 4. Participate in collection of common pests. 5. Find out more about possible side effects of eating contaminated produce.
resources.resources: 1. Samples of weeds common in the locality. 2. Charts and pictures showing control measures. 3. Fresh or preserved specimens of pests. 4. Specimen of maize, bean, guinea corn seeds infested by weevil, beetle or termite. 5. Chart showing local farm pests. 6. Insect-killing chemicals with warnings of poison clearly written. 7. Chart showing storage facilities.
resources.assessment: 1. State the meaning of weeds. 2. name three common weeds in the locality. 3. list two problems of weeds to farmers. 4. mention three control measures. 5. state the meaning of farm pests. 6. name five pests in the locality. 7. identify two damages caused by pests. 8. list three control measures of pests. 9. list three causal agents of crop diseases.

resources.title: Rearing of Farm Animal
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Needs of growing farm animals: - balanced ration - clean water - adequate - medication - clean environment. 2. Procedures for rearing farm animals: - construct a house or - provide shelter - provide necessary rearing equipment - buy the young animal - to rear. - provide feed and - water daily - provide medications - when necessary - clean the house - regularly - routine check by - veterinary personnel - removal of sick or - dead animals. - sell or slaughter when matured.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. state the needs of young animals for healthy growth. 2. mention steps involved in raising livestock. 3. describe how to raise a named farm animal. 4. identify and select appropriate housing and equipment for rearing: - Rabbits - guinea pigs - chicken 5. feed the livestock with the appropriate rations. 6. produce hutches, cages, brooder boxes for livestock.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses the needs of animals for healthy growth. 2. Guides the Pupils to rear any livestock and apply all the necessary skills. 3. Assists Pupils to select quality young animals e.g. young rabbit/young guinea pig, chicks for rearing. 4. Guides pupils to construct hutches. 5. Encourages Pupils to practice good sanitation and keep proper farm records. 6. Guides Pupils to identify sick animals, isolate them and invite a veterinary Doctor

Students: 1. Care for young animals by feeding, cleaning, providing water, beddings, etc. 2. Working in groups to care for the animals and apply necessary skills and procedures. 3. Observe and note the qualities of a healthy animal. 4. Collect different feed stuffs and feed the animal. 5. Clean the livestock area.
resources.resources: 1. School farm. 2. Balanced ration feed 3. Water 4. Medications 5. Animals to rear. 6. Shelter, etc. 7. Samples of pests/parasi te 8. Posters of sick animals.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list four necessary management practices required in rearing animals. 2. describe how to raise an animal farm to maturity. 3. construct good hutches and cages. 4. keep proper farm records. 5. identify two features of sick animal. 6. list three ways of controlling pests and diseases of farm animals. 7. narrate the effects of consuming infested animal products.

resources.title: Family: Functions, Relationships/ Tree, Family, Values and Life Cycle
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning, types and functions of the family. 2. Roles of each family member. 3. Family relationships and family tree; 4. Family life cycle: - the begining family - the expanding family - the contracting family. 5. Family values.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning and types of family; 2. list the functions of the family and the roles of family members; 3. decribe family relationship; and draw personal family tree; 4. explain the meaning of the family life cycle 5. enumerate family values.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on the meaning, types, and functions of the family. 2. Draws family tree on the board. 3. Explains the family tree. 4. Discusses family life cycle. 5. Discusses family values. 6. Displays a chart on family life cycle 7. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Explain the meaning of the family 2. Participate in the discussion of family and functions 3. Draw their personal family trees. 4. Participate in role playing of family relationships 5. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Family pictures 2. Chart on family free
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of family; 2. list three types of family. 3. state four types of relationshi ps in the family; 4. sketch a family tree; 5. state two family values.

resources.title: Uses of Personal and Family Resources
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning of resources 2. Personal resources: energy, time, personal belongings. 3. Family resources: money, house, properties etc. 4. Uses of personal and family resources. 5 Guidelines for care of personal belongings. 6. Care for personal belongings
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain meaning of resources; 2. itemize personal resources (eg belongings, energy, etc)and family resources (eg money, house); 3. explain the uses of personal and family resources; 4. state guidelines for caring for personal belongings; 5. care for personal belongings;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of personal and family resources. 2. Guides class discussion on personal and family resources 3. Presents pictures of some personal belongings 4. Demonstrates the steps of caring for personal belongings 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Identify and name personal and family resources. 2. State the uses of personal and family resources. 3. Participate in the discussion. 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Pictures and charts of some personal and family resources e.g. clothes, combs, money. 2. Some real objects e.g. clothes, plates, iron, radio
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define resources; 2. list four personal resources; 3. list five family resources; 4. state four guidelines for care of personal belongings.

resources.title: Types and Uses of Simple Sewing Tools and Equipment
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Simple sewing, knitting and crocheting tools and equipment. 2. Uses and care of simple sewing, knitting and crocheting tools. 3. Basic stitches 4. Common articles made by sewing, knitting and crocheting e.g. head-rest, tray cover, head band.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. list different types of sewing tools and equipment; 2. explain uses of sewing tools; 3. state the difference between sewing tools and equipment; 4. demonstrate the making of common articles e.g. stitches, running French scans
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays different sewing tools, types and sizes of sewing crocheting and knitting tools and equipment. 2. Discusses the uses and care of each tool and an equipment; 3. Demonstrates the use of each tool or equipment. 4. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Identify types of sewing tools or equipment. 2. Practice the use of sewing tools and equipment 3. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Sewing, knitting and crocheting tools and materials e.g. pins, wools, thread (assorted colours). 2. knitted sweater, crocheted articles e.g. table mats, head band. 3. Books on sewing, knitting and crocheting.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list three types of sewing equipment; 2. explain three uses of sewing tools.

resources.title: Cooking Tools and Equipment
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1 Identification of simple cooking tools and equipment. 2. Uses of cooking tools and equipment. 3. Guidelines for use of cooking tools and equipment. 4. Cleaning agents for cooking tools and equipment 5. Cleaning cooking tools and equipment 6. Demonstration on the use and care of each tools and equipment.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify tools and equipment for cooking 2. state the use(s) of each tool and equipment 3. differentiate between cooking tools and equipment 4. describe how to clean each tool and equipment. 5. practice how to handle each tool and equipment 6. clean cooking tools and equipment.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Differentiates between cooking tools and equipment 2. Brings samples of cooking tools and equipment 3. Guides the discussion on the uses of cooking tools and equipment. 4. Demonstrates how to use and clean each tool and equipment. 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in discussion. 2. Examine the cooking tools and equipment on display. 3. Clean cooking tools and equipment. 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Real objects. 2. Charts and picture showing cooking tools and equipment. 3. Utensils, e.g. frying spoons, knives, etc. 4. Cleaning agents for cooking tools and equipment.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify three cooking tools and two equipment. 2. differentiate between cooking tools and equipment 3. state two uses for any two tools and equipment; 4. give three guidelines for care of cooking tools and equipment; 5. list two cleaning agents for cooking tools and equipment. 6. demonstrate how to use simple tools and euipment.

resources.title: Food Safety and Cooking Methods
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Meaning of Food Safety. 2. Risk factors in raw food item contamination: - biological-mold, fungi, etc - chemical - pesticide, toxin,etc - physical - stone, metal rust, etc. 3. Meaning and reasons for cooking food. 4. Cooking methods: - boiling - steaming - stewing - frying - roasting - grilling - broiling 5. Advantages and disadvantages of each cooking method 6. Preparation of simple meals using different methods.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of food safety 2. discuss the risk factors in raw food items 3. explain the meaning and reason for cooking food 4. discuss the different cooking methods; 5. state advantages and disadvantages of each cooking method. 6. prepare foods using the different cooking methods.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines and explains the meaning and reasons of Food Safety. 2. Discusses the guide to Food Safety. 3. Guides discussion on different methods of cooking. 4. Demonstrates different meal preparation methods. 5. Supervises pupils practicals. 6. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in the discussions. 2. Copy the board summary 3. Practice at least one cooking method.
resources.resources: 1. Charts showing the different cooking methods. 2. Food ingredients for meal preparation 3. Cooking pot, stove, oven, frying pan, etc 4. Relevant books
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define and explain the meaning of food safety 2. list 5 five guides to food safety 3. mention three risk factors to food Ssafety 4. define cooking 5. state two reasons for cooking food 6. list five common methods of cooking; 7. mention three guidlines each for any three cooking methods; 8. cook using any method of cooking

resources.title: Preservation of Farm Produce
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Content: 1. Meaning of farm produce preservation. 2. Reasons for preservation of farm produce: - retain freshness, - reduce loss, - prolong shelf life, - prevent possible, contamination and infection from unpreserved food items 3. Methods of farms produce preservation: - sun-drying, - smoking, - salting, - frying, - refrigeration, - canning, - bagging, - bottling etc
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. state what farm produce preservation means. 2. give reasons why farm produce should be preserved. 3. state methods of farm produce preservation.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Provides beans and maize grains with holes and discuss why they have holes. 2. Guides Pupils to separate fresh from decaying spoilt food items (mouldy and decaying). 3. Guides Pupils to preserve food items using familiar method. 4. Ask Pupils to make a list of foods processed and preserved by members of the family. 5. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Observe and identify weeviled maize or beans. 2. Discuss reasons for preserving food items. 3. Observe procedure and do group practices of different preservation methods. 4. Make a list of foods processed and preserved by family members. 5. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. Weeviled unpreserved crops. 2. Preserved/ fresh grains. 3. Frozen meat or fish. 4. Bottled drink. 5. Canned meat, fish, milk etc. 6. Food items for preservation: - meat, fish, grains, cassava, yams, etc. 7. Posters or charts showing the different methods of food preservation e.g. people frying/ smoking/ drying fish
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define and explain food preservation. 2. state four reasons for preserving farms produce items. 3. list five methods of farm produce preservation.

resources.title: Packaging Methods
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Content: 1. Why package farm produce?: - to make produce appealing to buyers, - for ease of transportation, - for proper identification, 2. Packaging items: - cans, - cellophane wrappers, - cardboard boxes, - baskets, - - cages.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. give reasons why farm produce are packaged 2. identify packaging materials
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Produce some agricultural packaging for local farm produce 2. Explains reasons for packaging. 3. Provides packaging items. 4. Give a board summary

Students: 1.Partake in the production of packaging items for fruits and vegetables, eggs, poultry chick 2. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. canned food 2. Sun-dried foods 3. smoked produce 4. fried food etc. 5. local packaging materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. give 3 reasons for packaging produce 2. list 5 packaging items used in agriculture

resources.title: Marketing and Farm Records
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING, MARKETING AND FARM RECORDS | Content: 1. Definition of market and marketing 2. Agricultural marketing activities 3. Types of markets for agricultural produce 4. Meaning of farm record. 5. Types of farm records: - farm diary - cash record - production record 6. Uses of farm record - to know items in the farm. - quantity of farm produce realized - amount of money realized from sales 7. Record Keeping: - daily diary of events on the farm.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define marketing 2. explain marketing activities in agriculture, 3. state the types of agricultural markets. 4. define farm records 5. list farm records. 6. state the uses of farm records. 7. keep good farm records.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides classroom discussion. 2. Guides pupils to write proper and correct records of activities in their note books(diary) 3. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Classroom discussion 2. Record all activities in the farm diary 3. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. Real agricultural product in the localities. 2. Charts of agricultural products. 3. Charts of simple farm records
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state what is meant by a market 2. give simple explanation of marketing. 3. list three agricultural marketing activities. 4. mention four types of agricultural markets. 5. define farm records. 6. list three types of record that can be kept in the farm. 7. state four uses of farm records. 8. record the activities carried out on the school farm.

resources.title: Healthy Home Environment
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Reasons for cleaning the home, classroom and environment 2. Tools and agents for cleaning the home 3. Guidelines for cleaning the home and its surroundings 4. Processes for cleaning the home eg-dusting, sweeping, washing, scrubbing, etc. 5. Application of processes
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. state reasons for cleaning their homes, classroom and home and school environment 2. list tools and agents for cleaning the home and its surroundings 3. state guidelines for cleaning the home and its surroundings 4. describe processes for cleaniing the home and surroun dings 5. clean their rooms/ classroom.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on reasons, cleaning tools, and agents, guidelines and processes for cleaning the home, classroom and surroundings. 2. Demonstrates the cleaning processes. 3. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion. 2. Bring cleaning materials 3. Practice cleaning of room/classroom and environment 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: Tool and agents for cleaning different parts of a room: e.g. broom, water, buckets, mop, brushes, detergents, towels, dust bin, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention three reasons for cleaning the home and surrounding 2. list five tools for cleaning the home. 3. state three guidelines for cleaning a room. 4. clean the classroom/ toilet

resources.title: Stitches: Types and Uses
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Meaning of stitches. 2. Types of stitch and their uses, e.g. temporary, permanent and decorative stitches. 3. Guidelines of making different types of stitch. 4. Production of articles with different types of decorative stitches.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define stitches 2. classify types of stitch 3. state the general uses of stitches 4. describe the steps in making both temporary, permanent and decorative stitches 5. produce articles using the different types of stitch.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of stitches 2. Lists the different classes of stitch. 3. Demonstrates the process of making temporary, permanent and decorative stitches. 4. Use different types of stitch in producing food cover, pillow slips/cases, head band. 5. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Practice the making of temporary, permanent and decorative stitches. 3. Produce articles using different stitches. 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Charts showing stages of making stitches 2. Pieces of fabrics for making stitches 3. Sewing tools e.g. needles, pins, tapes 4. An album showing stages of making temporary, permanent and decorative stitches.
resources.assessment: Pupils should: 1. define stitches 2. identify the classes and types of stitch 3. state three uses of stitches; 4. describe the steps in making stitches 5. make specimens of temporary, permanent and decorative stitches.

resources.title: Clothing Construction Process
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILES | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILES | Content: 1. Meaning of seam; 2. Types of seam e.g. - plain/open seam; - run and fell seam; - french seam; 3. Uses of seams; 4. Steps in making the different seams; 5. Making seams on brown paper
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define seam and mention types of seam. 2. state uses of seam 3. describe the steps for making seams 4. produce an lbum showing stages of making seams
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines a seam; 2. Discusses types of seam; 3. Exhibits different types of seam; 4. Discusses uses of seams; 5. Discuss the stages of making seams; 6. Demonstrates the steps in making of seams, 7. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Examine seams exhibited by the teacher; 2. Practice how to make seams on brown paper following teacher’s demonstation; 3. Copy board the summary.
resources.resources: 1. Different garments showing different seams; 2. Charts showing stages of seam making 3. Album showing samples of stages of seam making 4. Brown paper, coloured threads, scissors, needles, pins, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain the meaning of seam, 2. name two types of seam, 3. state three uses of seams 4. produce an album showing the steps of plain seam run and fell seams, french seam 5. produce needle work bag for display.

resources.title: Meal Planning for Healthy Living
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Meaning of meal planning; 2. importance and guidelines for healthy eating 3. Effects of wrong meal planning and Eating Habit 4. Three Major meals of the day; 5. Factors to consider in planning meal 6. Guidelines for meal planning; 7. Menu cards.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of meal planning and eating for healthy living; 2. discuss the importance and guidelines for healthy eating; 3. state factors influencing meal planning 4. identify the right foods for the three meals of the day; 5. plan a simple breakfast, lunch and supper/dinner; 6. write a menu card.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains: a) meaning of meal planning b) importance and guidelines for healthy eating 2. Explains factors that influence meal planning 3. Discusses the three major meals of the day. 4. Explains the effects of wrong meal planning. 5. Mentions the guidelines in meal planning 6. Plans meal with pupils. 7. Gives a chalkboard summary.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions; 2. explain the effect of healthy and unhealthy eating habits. 3. Plan a day’s meal; 4. Write menu card. 5. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Chart showing the food groups 2. Charts on food nutrients 3. Charts showing various meal plans 4. Simple menu cards 5. Pictures of obese children and adults
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of meal planning; 2. state four guidelines for healthy eating 3. name the three meals of a day; 4. state two guidelines for meal planning 5. list the factors that influence meal planning 6. Plan a day’s menu for a family.

resources.title: Kitchen: Definition, Types
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Meaning of kitchen and types: 2. Different types of kitchen layout or plans or arrangement. 3. Reasons for cleaning kitchens (kitchen hygiene): - to avoid household pests, odour and accidents - to prevent diseases. 4. Home accidents 5. Content of a First Aid Box and their uses. 6. Guidelines for kitchen hygiene and prevention of home accidents.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define a kitchen 2. explain types of kitchen 3. describe different types of kitchen arrangement 4. mention the reasons for maintaining kitchen hygiene 5. discuss common accidents in the kitchen 6. list the contents of a First Aid Box
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses types of kitchen arrangement, reasons for cleaning in a kitchen. 2. Demonstrates processes of cleaning a kitchen 3. Discusses the content of the First Aid Box and their uses. 4. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion; 2. Participate in cleaning a kitchen; 3. Help in preparing a First Aid Box for the class; 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Materials for making a First Aid Box 2. Chart showing First Aid Box items 3. Pictures of traditional and modern kitchen 4. Chart on kitchen plan/ arrangement 5. Mop, floor cloth, mop- bucket, soap, water, scrubbing brush, long and short broom, dust pan and trash bin, 6. Towels, napkins, apron, cap, head- tie.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define kitchen 2. list two types of kitchen 3. mention two types of kitchen plan/arrange ment. 4. give two reasons for cleaning a kitchen. 5. mention five items used in cleaning a kitchen. 6. mention five items found in a First Aid Box.
